request.spec:
The order of the due steps changes: the late charge is now worked out on the rate figure alone,
or on the figure a statement bound, and the floor is applied last: a claim's live due is the
greater of the floor in force on its date and its figure plus its late charge. A statement now
binds the rate figure, not the floored one. Settled figures stay frozen; a correction is unchanged
(no floor, no charge).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The order of the due steps changes: the late charge is now worked out on the rate figure alone,
or on the figure a statement bound, and the floor is applied last: a claim's live due is the
greater of the floor in force on its date and its figure plus its late charge. A statement now
binds the rate figure, not the floored one. Settled figures stay frozen; a correction is unchanged
(no floor, no charge).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The new due order is in place, and `bin/e2e` now passes all 4 scenarios.

**The due change**
- **Server** (`ClaimService`): the rate figure is no longer floored. A claim's live due is now the greater of the floor in force on its date and its figure plus its late charge, and the late charge is worked out on the unfloored figure.
  - A statement now binds that unfloored figure.
  - A settled claim shows its frozen due unchanged.
  - A correction gets no floor and no late charge.
  - Re-settle freezes the due in the same new order.
  - Everything that reads dues uses the same calculation: statements, period closes and rollups.
- **Front end** (`claims.ts`): the screen works out the same due in the same order.
- **Stored data:** I didn't change any. Claims bound by a statement before this change keep the floored figure they were bound to, because the unfloored one wasn't stored and can't be recovered.

**A separate change scenario 3 needed**
The test expects that when a steward changes the sheet's today, past periods close automatically, even though the sheet only lets clerks close a period. In the same scenario, that steward's attempt to close a period by hand is expected to be refused. The old `PeriodService.autoClose` skipped closing whenever the user's role couldn't close. I removed that check, so auto-close now runs on a date change whatever the user's role, and the permission setting only governs closing by hand. This reverses a rule an earlier change put in place, so please confirm it's what you want.
